registry.description: Shame is the painful inner awareness of being exposed as inadequate, wrong, or unworthy — and the accompanying fear of rejection or contempt. The Hebrew vocabulary is extensive and connected to honour and disgrace: to be shamed is to be publicly diminished, stripped of one's standing. The body is fully implicated: the face falls or is covered, the person wants to disappear. God is said to put to shame those who oppose his people, and to honour those who hope in him. Shame is addressed most directly in the gospel: the one who trusts in him will not be put to shame.
